item: row 426: an import refused before its swap removes the safety copy it made itself (R833)
key_paths: src/backup/own_net.py src/backup/merge.py src/backup/import_queue.py src/safety/data_scope.py src/static/app-backup.js tests/test_refused_run_safety_copy.py
summary: A run refused before activation removes only its own safety copy: known by path and (dev, inode, size, mtime, ctime) recorded when made, never a name pattern; only when the durable record import-safety-copies.json says made (activated, missing or unreadable keeps it; the in-memory record is dropped first at the swap); only when the live corpus is the same file with the same size, mtime, first 100 bytes and -wal state, read through the R789-safe reader and kept as an HMAC under a process key (R828: no header byte is written anywhere). An ordinary no-follow delete of a regular file in the data folder through the folder handle, worded safety copy removed: the import was refused before any change. A queue run settles at its end before the search-index tuning writes; a lone restore when it ends. Nothing runs at a start: a crash leaves the copy, and the import report lists the copies left in the data folder by count and total size.
